questions.text: Cell-culture antiviral activity prompted trials; later experiments linked this activity to membrane disruption at concentrations above reported toxic clinical concentrations.

questions.title: What is the ovarian-cancer hypothesis?
questions.text: Ivermectin inhibited PAK1, a growth-signaling kinase, and suppressed growth of ovarian cancer cell lines.

questions.title: Why combine it with sorafenib in liver cancer?
questions.text: Preclinical experiments tested whether simultaneous interference with growth pathways could strengthen sorafenib-associated cancer-cell death.

questions.title: Testing the WNT–TCF explanation
questions.text: In colorectal-cancer experiments, forcing TCF signaling back on rescued cells from some low-concentration ivermectin effects. Ivermectin also inhibited TCF-dependent mouse xenografts but not a TCF-independent comparison model. This is stronger mechanistic evidence than an association between a pathway marker and cell death. Its relevance still depends on tumor biology, exposure and formulation; it does not establish clinical cancer benefit.

questions.title: What do the original in vitro antiviral results show about concentrations?
questions.text: A 2020 cell-culture experiment found ivermectin suppressed SARS-CoV-2 replication in Vero-hSLAM cells, which is a preclinical in vitro finding. A human dose-escalation pharmacokinetic study characterizing plasma exposures at escalating doses, and later mechanistic work, together indicate that in vitro antiviral activity was observed at concentrations that exceeded plasma levels reported in human subjects, including at high investigational doses. This concentration gap means the in vitro result does not translate directly to clinical antiviral activity.

questions.title: What SARS-CoV-2 molecular targets has ivermectin been proposed to act on?
questions.text: In vitro and in silico mechanistic studies have proposed that ivermectin may disrupt the importin alpha/beta1 heterodimer complex involved in nuclear transport of viral proteins, inhibit the viral 3CLpro main protease, and interact with the spike protein active site. These are proposed mechanisms identified in cell-based and computational models; they have not been confirmed as drivers of clinical benefit, and randomized trials of ivermectin for COVID-19 have not shown patient benefit.

guides.description: An antiparasitic with negative randomized COVID-19 findings and laboratory cancer research.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Oral ivermectin is used for strongyloidiasis and onchocerciasis. A higher-dose COVID-19 trial did not speed recovery; the cancer studies discussed here are preclinical.

sentences.text: Oral ivermectin is used for strongyloidiasis and onchocerciasis.
A higher-dose COVID-19 trial did not speed recovery; the cancer studies discussed here are preclinical.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: Six days of higher-dose ivermectin did not improve sustained recovery from acute COVID-19. Ovarian, brain, breast and colorectal cancer experiments reported effects in cells or animals, without a patient benefit estimate from those experiments. The liver-cancer combination report is retracted and excluded from efficacy conclusions.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Reported harms include dizziness, low blood pressure, serious skin reactions and neurotoxicity; heavy Loa loa infection can increase the risk of severe encephalopathy.

questions.question: Is ivermectin safe at higher doses?
questions.answer: A dose-escalation study in healthy adults and a systematic review and meta-analysis of high-dose regimens support that ivermectin was tolerated at doses above the standard labeled range, with generally transient adverse effects. These findings describe investigational research regimens and do not constitute a recommendation for off-label high-dose use.

sentences.text: A dose-escalation study in healthy adults and a systematic review and meta-analysis of high-dose regimens support that ivermectin was tolerated at doses above the standard labeled range, with generally transient adverse effects.
These findings describe investigational research regimens and do not constitute a recommendation for off-label high-dose use.

questions.question: Is ivermectin safe during pregnancy and lactation?
questions.answer: A systematic review and meta-analysis of inadvertent pregnancy exposures did not identify a significantly elevated risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes. A later cluster-randomized trial analysis examining periconception ivermectin exposure similarly did not find a clear increase in adverse outcomes. The US prescribing information notes that the safety of ivermectin in pregnant women has not been established.
